:::{#thm-incompressible-strings}
#### Most strings are incompressible

Let $n \ge 1$ and $0 \le k \le n$ be integers.
Fewer than $2^{n-k}$ of the $2^n$ binary strings of length $n$ satisfy
$K(x \mid n) < n - k$.
In particular, at least one string of length $n$ has $K(x \mid n) \ge n$.

:::

::: {.proof}
There are $2^j$ binary strings of length $j$,
so the number of programs of length less than $n - k$ is

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n-k-1} 2^j = 2^{n-k} - 1,$$

where the sum is empty, and equal to $0$, when $k = n$.

Given $n$, each program outputs at most one string,
so at most $2^{n-k} - 1$ strings $x$ have a program shorter than $n - k$.
With $k = 0$, at most $2^n - 1$ of the $2^n$ strings of length $n$
have $K(x \mid n) < n$, which leaves at least one with $K(x \mid n) \ge n$.

:::
